description:
FILED s432 (Opus 5), measured while shipping #456 half (a) (a forward-declaration stub that is CALLED now dies instead of answering nil).

THE SAME CHANGE, THE SAME MECHANISM, TWO POPULATIONS:

  * perl-tests sweep (sweep-perl-tests.pl): loads the emitted CL with
    `pcl::p-load-with-recovery`, which evaluates ONE top-level form at a time and
    recovers from an uncaught die in any single form.  Cost of the change: ONE
    row (sort.t 203 -> 202), the form that died.
  * companion suite (tools/run-perl-suite.pl, line ~601): plain `--load`.  One
    die ends the file.  Cost of the SAME change: op/method.t 96 -> 44,
    op/sort.t 181 -> 142, op/lexsub.t 9 -> 6 (op/gmagic.t 0 -> 1) = -94 rows,
    every one of them AFTER the dying form in files that already crash.

So a per-file row count from the companion suite is not comparable to one from
the sweep for any change that makes something die, and the difference is the
RUNNER, not PCL.  That is the same class of trap as #324 (one runner measuring
on a 2 MB stack for months) and the reason CLAUDE.md made the five runners share
one SBCL command-line builder -- recovery is a second axis they do not share.

DO: give tools/run-perl-suite.pl the same `p-load-with-recovery` load (it is a
one-line change to the sbcl command at line ~601), then RE-BLESS the companion
snapshot in one measured pass, because every file that currently dies mid-way
will report more rows.  That re-bless is the reason this is a task and not a
drive-by: the snapshot's rows are the comparison baseline for every future
session, so the change and the re-bless must land together, with the diff
explained per file.

ALTERNATIVE to weigh first: recovery makes the companion suite report rows perl
would never reach either, so it can turn a hard failure into a partial pass and
hide a regression.  The sweep already accepts that trade (its rows carry the
INCOMPLETE note).  Whichever way it goes, the two runners should AGREE, and the
choice belongs in one place.


=== s433 (Fable) RULING: DO IT -- recovery in BOTH runners; the re-bless of docs/perl-suite-run.tsv lands in the SAME commit, one measured pass (--all, once), every moved file explained (files that died mid-way report MORE rows; a file reporting FEWER is a finding).  Rule goes into docs/test-infrastructure.md.  Users (runpcl) stay plain load.  Same session (Q1 of plan-post-s433): the missing-snapshot-row report (the five s431 rows were found by counting; the runner must print files with no row) + #462.  Q1 is the precondition of the flip (Q2) and of #456(b) (Q3): their companion legs must measure FORMS, not files.


=== s434 (Opus 5, 2026-08-22) DONE.  tools/run-perl-suite.pl now spawns `--eval (pcl::p-load-with-recovery "F")` instead of `--load F`; a recovered form is counted and printed as `aborted-forms:N: <condition>` BEFORE the status decision (so such a file can never read as OK), and a reader stop as `unreadable-form:`.  docs/perl-suite-run.tsv re-blessed in the same commit from one --all --jobs 4 pass plus the #366 serial discipline (the runner's cap dropped 22 movers; they were re-run in a second --jobs 1 pass): 52 files GAINED rows, 0 lost, TOTAL C_ok 74803 -> 77128 (+2325), 116 signature-only changes.  Two status movers and one signature loss measured PRE-EXISTING against a 4356e77 worktree; uni/variables.t's flood attributed TO the change by the same A/B.  The six #326 hang-set rows are stopwatch readings (contention cost them 300-400 rows in the parallel pass; alone they land at their blessed values).  docs/perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv re-blessed for SIX registered files that now reach rows they used to die before.  Rule written into docs/test-infrastructure.md.
subject: The two populations' runners DISAGREE on per-form recovery: the sweep loads the generated CL with p-load-with-recovery, tools/run-perl-suite.pl with a plain --load -- so one die costs 1 row in one population and 94 in the other
